questions.question: During a shrinkage test per ISO 3380, an operator increases the heating rate to 8.0 °C/min instead of the mandated 2.0 ± 0.2 °C/min. How will this procedural error affect the recorded shrinkage temperature (Ts)?

answers.a: The recorded Ts will be artificially elevated due to thermal lag between the rapidly heating water bath and the interior core of the leather strip
answers.b: The recorded Ts will be significantly lower because collagen dissolves faster at higher heating rates
answers.c: There will be no effect because shrinkage temperature is a thermodynamic constant independent of heating kinetics
answers.d: The leather strip will expand by 200% instead of shrinking

questions.question: A vegetable-tanned leather specimen strip with an initial gauge length L₀ = 50.0 mm is subjected to the shrinkage test. After complete hydrothermal denaturation, the final contracted length Lf is measured as 36.5 mm. What is the percentage longitudinal shrinkage (%S)?
Why does ISO 3380 require testing duplicate specimen strips cut both parallel and perpendicular to the backbone (lines of toughness)?

answers.a: To verify that the weighing scale does not drift over time
answers.b: Because collagen fiber bundles exhibit natural directional anisotropy in alignment and density relative to the animal's spine, potentially causing directional variations in hydrothermal response
answers.c: To ensure that the dye coloring on both sides of the hide is identical
answers.d: Because one orientation measures apparent density while the other measures tensile modulus

questions.question: In a laboratory test, two duplicate strips of vegetable-tanned sole leather yield shrinkage temperatures of 82.5 °C (parallel to backbone) and 83.5 °C (perpendicular to backbone). What is the reported mean shrinkage temperature (Ts,mean)?

When testing a high-grade Chrome-Tanned Upper Leather (Wet Blue) sample in distilled water, the bath temperature reaches 100.0 °C (boiling point at standard atmospheric pressure) and the indicator pointer exhibits 0.0 mm deflection. What is the standard technical conclusion?

answers.a: The test has failed and the apparatus must be discarded
answers.b: The leather satisfies the hydrothermal boiling test criterion (Ts > 100.0 °C), indicating complete, stable chromium cross-linking
answers.c: The leather has zero degree of tannage and must be retanned
answers.d: The water used was contaminated with salt ions

questions.question: Why cannot an open-bath distilled water apparatus be utilized to determine the exact numerical shrinkage temperature of wet blue leathers that shrink above 100 °C?

answers.b: Water boils and vaporizes at 100.0 °C under atmospheric pressure, limiting open bath temperature unless a high-boiling medium (e.g. 75:25 glycerol:water) or a sealed pressurized hydrothermal cell is used
answers.c: The glass beaker will shatter at 101 °C
answers.d: Magnetic stir bars lose their magnetic dipole alignment above 95 °C

questions.question: If a newly developed 'wet white' leather batch exhibits a shrinkage temperature of only 66.0 °C, what does this indicate regarding the tanning process?

answers.a: Excellent over-tannage with superior thermal stability
answers.b: Severe under-tannage or insufficient cross-linking density, barely exceeding that of untanned pelt (60–65 °C), making it unsuitable for shoe upper molding
answers.c: The presence of excessive chromium trichloride crystals
answers.d: Ideal tanning characteristics for military boot outsoles

questions.question: What exact visual/physical indicator defines the onset of hydrothermal shrinkage during observation of the graduated scale?

answers.a: The pointer rapidly oscillating back and forth randomly
answers.b: The first distinct, continuous, and steady displacement of the pointer indicating specimen shortening
answers.c: The appearance of small water bubbles on the glass wall
answers.d: The instant the water bath changes color from clear to brown

questions.question: In footwear manufacturing, why is a high hydrothermal shrinkage temperature (Ts ≥ 100 °C) essential for shoe upper leathers?

answers.a: To allow the shoes to be cleaned with industrial bleach
answers.b: To withstand direct vulcanization, hot-melt adhesive curing, toe-puff molding, and hot iron ironing/finishing without grain puckering, curling, or thermal contraction
answers.c: To eliminate the requirement for lining materials inside shoes
answers.d: To increase the total electrical resistance of safety boots to 1000 MΩ

questions.question: If an operator replaces the recommended 3.0 g counterweight with a 100.0 g weight, what error is introduced into the shrinkage temperature determination?

answers.a: The water bath will heat up twice as fast
answers.b: Excessive mechanical tensile stress will cause premature plastic creep and fiber elongation, distorting the genuine hydrothermal contraction threshold and potentially snapping the strip
answers.c: The true collagen denaturation temperature will increase by 50 °C
answers.d: Chromium ions will be forced back into the aqueous solution
